newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firmer, but futures rally loses steam.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, but futures rally loses steam.

text.p: Asian crude prices firmed sharply on Tuesday in line with a strong overnight rally in futures prices.

However, the rally was coming under pressure in early London after SIMEX had added a few cents. June SIMEX Brent ended one cent higher at $19.73, but at 0945 GMT, the contract was down nine cents in London at $19.63.
June paper Tapis, the most active month, responded by adding 40 cents to trade several times at $21.00.
The market was quoted at $20.90/$21.15 in late afternoon dealings.
However, the rally sparked little fresh physical activity as June Middle East trading comes to an end and players wait for regional dealings for June to start.
A producer sold 170,000 barrels of June Labuan at published Tapis quotes plus 50/55 cents per barrel, in line with the market. The buyer was an unnamed Singapore refiner.
A cargo of Oman crude for June was heard traded at Dubai quotes plus 80 cents and may have been part of a swap arrangement, although details were initially sketchy.
Murban was heard traded for June at ADNOC -25 cents, adding confusion to prices after a recent deal heard at -13 cents.
The latest deal was between a French major a a large South Korean refiner for 130,000 barrels.

No real price talk was emerging yet for the July market, although players said they expected a further discount market owing to the seasonally low demand for regional June barrels and Middle East July barrels.
